question: What is the correct sequence for performing an abdominal physical examination?
explanation: Auscultation is done before palpation and percussion so the examiner does not alter bowel motility and sounds before listening to them. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is palpation performed last during a standard abdominal assessment?

options.A: It ensures the bladder is completely empty
options.B: It prevents altering normal bowel sounds
options.C: It is the most painful part of the exam
options.D: It allows the patient time to relax fully

explanation: Touching or pushing on the abdomen early in the exam can stimulate peristalsis, creating false bowel sound readings during auscultation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h1)

question: Prolonged vomiting from a gastrointestinal obstruction typically leads to which acid-base imbalance?
explanation: Loss of gastric hydrochloric acid through vomiting removes acid from the body, leaving an excess of bicarbonate and causing metabolic alkalosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h2)

question: A patient with severe watery diarrhea for three days is at greatest risk for developing what condition?
explanation: Lower gastrointestinal fluids are rich in bicarbonate, so excessive loss from diarrhea depletes base buffers and results in metabolic acidosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h2)

question: Enteral nutrition is preferred over parenteral nutrition for a functioning GI tract because it maintains what?
explanation: Feeding directly into the GI tract preserves the structure and immune function of the intestinal mucosa, preventing bacterial translocation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: Total parenteral nutrition requires a central venous access device primarily for what reason?

options.A: The high concentration of nutrients irritates peripheral veins
options.B: Central lines deliver fluids twice as fast as peripheral lines
options.C: Patients cannot tolerate peripheral needles during bowel rest
options.D: Infection rates are significantly lower with central access

explanation: TPN solutions are hypertonic and can cause sclerosis and inflammation in smaller peripheral vessels, requiring dilution in a large central vein. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which nursing intervention helps relieve abdominal distension and discomfort in a patient with a bowel obstruction?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the abdomen
options.B: Placing the patient flat on their back
options.C: Maintaining patency of a nasogastric tube

explanation: A patent nasogastric tube continuously decompresses the stomach and upper bowel, removing gas and fluid that cause painful distension. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is careful assessment of acute abdominal pain essential before administering strong pain medications?

options.A: Patients with GI issues cannot metabolize standard analgesics
options.B: Masking symptoms can delay the diagnosis of surgical emergencies
options.C: Analgesics stop the absorption of all oral antibiotics
options.D: Opioids always cause permanent bowel paralysis

explanation: Administering powerful painkillers too early can hide critical warning signs of acute conditions like appendicitis or perforation, delaying necessary surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h4)

question: When is the best time for a patient to take a prescribed proton pump inhibitor?

options.A: Before the first meal of the day
options.D: Right before going to sleep at night

explanation: Proton pump inhibitors are most effective when taken before the first meal because food triggers the activation of proton pumps in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why should antidiarrheal medications be withheld when a patient has an acute bacterial infection of the bowel?

options.A: These drugs cause immediate and severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: Bacterial pathogens become resistant to antibiotics when slowed down
options.C: Antidiarrheals neutralize the effectiveness of prescribed intravenous fluids
options.D: Slowing motility traps toxins and infectious organisms in the body

explanation: Stoppage of bowel movements prevents the body from expelling harmful bacteria and toxins, potentially worsening systemic infection. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: What clinical sign indicates the return of bowel motility after abdominal surgery?
explanation: The passage of flatus or a bowel movement is the most reliable clinical indicator that peristalsis has resumed throughout the intestinal tract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of encouraging early ambulation following gastrointestinal surgery?

options.A: Ensuring immediate tolerance of a regular diet
options.B: Accelerating the complete healing of internal anastomoses
options.C: Preventing venous stasis and pulmonary complications
options.D: Eliminating the need for postoperative pain medication

explanation: Moving around promotes blood circulation in the lower extremities to prevent clots and expands lung capacity to prevent atelectasis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h6)

question: A rigid, board-like abdomen in a patient with a GI disorder is a classic sign of what emergency?
explanation: Inflammation of the peritoneal lining from a rupture or leak causes involuntary muscle guarding, resulting in a rigid, board-like abdomen. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h7)

question: Dumping syndrome after gastric surgery is primarily managed through what dietary adjustment?

options.A: Increasing intake of concentrated glucose beverages
options.B: Lying flat immediately after consuming meals
options.C: Drinking large volumes of fluid during meals
options.D: Eating smaller, frequent meals low in simple sugars

explanation: Limiting simple carbohydrates and separating liquids from solids prevents rapid gastric emptying into the small intestine. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h7)

question: Before discharge, what is the best way to verify that a patient can manage a new ostomy appliance?

options.A: Asking if they understand the steps explained
options.B: Having the patient perform a return demonstration
options.C: Handing them an illustrated instructional booklet
options.D: Showing a video demonstration in the room

explanation: A return demonstration allows the nurse to directly observe the patient's skill and correct any technique errors before they go home. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of comprehensive discharge planning for a patient with a chronic GI condition?

options.A: Eliminating all future need for follow-up clinic visits
options.B: Transitioning the patient to permanent total parenteral nutrition
options.C: Reducing hospital costs through early removal of medications
options.D: Ensuring safe self-management and preventing readmission

explanation: Good discharge planning equips the patient with the knowledge and skills needed to care for themselves successfully outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h8)
